historical_references.reference: The name 'Nahar' is believed to have been used for the river Nahr el-Kelb in Lebanon during the Umayyad Caliphate. According to some historians, the caliph Al-Walid I (705-715 CE) built a palace on the banks of this river and named it 'Nahar' after the Arabic word for 'river'.
historical_references.context: Construction of a palace by Al-Walid I along the Nahr el-Kelb in Lebanon and its subsequent naming as 'Nahar'.

historical_references.reference: The name 'Nahar' is also associated with the Islamic colony in Brazil, founded in 1624 CE, which was known as 'Nahar El-Bred'. This name is believed to have been derived from the Arabic word 'nahar' meaning 'river', and 'el-Bred' meaning 'of the bread', due to the settlers' reliance on the land for farming and subsistence.
historical_references.context: Foundation of the Islamic colony in Brazil called 'Nahar El-Bred' derived from the Arabic word 'nahar' meaning 'river' and 'el-Bred' meaning 'of the bread'.
